dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you?
Hi Kevin. Well, if you need a boat, I know a street that's got room for one. Sorry, you're on speaker, I'm walking around and my tool belt won't stop jingling. Can you hear me okay?
I hear you fine, jingle and all. What's going on?

So I'm at 311 Ayrault Street, up on the Hill. After that coastal storm Friday and Saturday, two days ago, the street in front of my house is basically a pond. It's still sitting there. And every car that goes by throws a wake right up onto my front walk.
Okay, 311 Ayrault. Standing water in the roadway out front. Is it up over the curb, or just filling the street?

Both, kind of. It's over the gutter and halfway up the curb. The drain at the corner is just sitting there, I can't see it at all. Nothing's going down. [pause] Hang on, let me step outside the door so you can hear me better.
Sure, no rush. I'm writing this down. Standing water, drain at the corner not taking anything.
Okay, I'm back. Okay. Here's my thing. I called about this a while ago, and somebody told me that Ayrault is a state road. So, not the city's problem. That's what I got.

Right, I see why you'd remember that. Some roads in town do belong to the state, and those get handled by the state's highway people. I'm not sure that's true for that stretch of Ayrault, so I want to check on it with our crew supervisor instead of just passing you along.
I would appreciate that, because I'm going back and forth between two offices and the water is not moving. It's wet, it's cold, and now it's starting to get slushy on the edges.
Yeah, that'll turn into ice overnight if it keeps sitting there. Is it blocking anybody's driveway or is it just the street?
Just the street so far. My neighbor's got a little dip in her driveway and it's right at the edge. Cars slow down, but some people just plow through. [crosstalk] Sorry, go ahead.
No, you go. I was going to ask if there's leaves or trash packed on the grate, or if you can't see it.
Can't see it. Maybe there's leaves, I really can't tell. The water's about, I don't know, six inches deep at the deepest part by the grate. I'm not wading in to find out.

Good call, don't. Okay. So I've got 311 Ayrault Street, Historic Hill, drain at the corner appears blocked or overwhelmed, water over the gutter and up the curb since the storm, and a previous note that you were told it was a state road. Did I get that right?
That's it. Pretty much word for word.

Good. What I'll do is send this to the supervisor and ask two things. Is that section city or state, and if it's ours, can a crew get out there and clear the drain. If it turns out to be state, I'll find out who to hand it to so you're not starting over.
That would be great. Because honestly, the last time, I just hung up and figured that was the end of it. Nobody said who to call or anything.
Yeah, that's not much help. I'll make sure it's in the notes this time. Can I get a number for you?
Zero one eight eight. Got it. Is this a good number during the day?

Yeah, that's my cell. I'm on and off job sites, so if I miss it, leave a message. And Kevin, can you have somebody call me back when it's done? I don't need a play by play. Just call me when somebody's been out, or when you've figured out whose street it is.

Absolutely. I'll put in the note to call you back once it's resolved or handed off. I can't tell you exactly when a crew will get there, since they've got a long list after a storm like that, but I'll mark it as standing water in the road with it freezing up.
Okay. I get that. I'm just saying, it's two days. Seems like long enough.
Understood. It does, especially with temps dropping tonight. I'll flag that.
Thanks. And if anybody's coming out, tell them to watch for the wake. The cars out here are not slowing down.
I'll add that in. Anything else going on at the house, or just the drain?
Just the drain. Everything else is fine, it's staying out of the house at least.
Good. Okay Ms. Cabral, you're all set on my end. You'll hear from somebody. Take care out there.
You too, Kevin. Thanks.
